anomalies.observed: On sheet /NFC_IC/ the NT3H2111's supply pin U3 pin 6 ('VCC') is wired down and to the right so that it lands on the LOWER terminal of C8, the node that the bypass capacitor's ground side occupies; C8's UPPER terminal is attached to a 'VCC' power symbol. U3 pin 7 (VOUT) is separately tied to its own 'VCC' symbol, so only pin 6 is on the wrong node.
anomalies.expected: U3 pin 6 must be on the VCC net together with U3 pin 7 (VOUT) and the board VCC rail, with C8 connected between VCC and GND as a 100 nF local bypass capacitor.

evidence.quote: Sheet /NFC_IC/ (page 2): U3 pin '6 VCC' connects by a wire running down and right to the lower terminal of 'C8 100n', while C8's upper terminal is attached to a 'VCC' power symbol.
U3's `VOUT` (energy-harvesting output, pin 7) is tied to the same `VCC` net as its own `VCC` pin (pin 6) and the board's main VCC rail.
C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C8 — 100 nF each, VCC–GND (local bypass)

anomalies.impact: The NT3H2111's VCC pin is tied to the capacitor's ground-side node instead of the VCC rail, so the NFC tag IC's supply pin has no VCC connection (it sits on the GND node of C8), and the MCU will not be able to communicate with the tag over the NFC_SDA/NFC_SCL I2C bus.

parsed.summary: The drawing otherwise matches the specification (MCU pinout, NFC/display sheet wiring, TSC R8/C14, decoupling values, OLED charge-pump network), but on the NFC sheet the NT3H2111's VCC pin (U3.6) is wired to the lower, ground-side terminal of its decoupling capacitor C8 instead of to the VCC rail, leaving the NFC IC's supply pin off the VCC net.
